mechanisms.name: TP all-reduce backend selection
mechanisms.trigger: every tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce in a model forward on TP > 1
mechanisms.observable: each rank picks one backend per tensor, in order: NCCL symm-mem, QuickReduce, FlashInfer PCIe IPC, FlashInfer, AITER, custom all-reduce, batch-invariant ROCm, torch symm-mem, PyNccl, torch.distributed; the output is the same sum at different latency
mechanisms.note: The NVIDIA path runs as FlashInfer, then symm-mem, custom, torch symm-mem or PyNccl. QuickReduce, FlashInfer PCIe IPC, AITER and the batch-invariant branches are missing, the model tests FlashInfer before NCCL symm-mem where the code only excludes it, and should-custom-ar skips the weak-contiguous check.

mechanisms.name: Custom all-reduce setup gates and IPC buffers
mechanisms.trigger: CudaCommunicator construction on a TP group
mechanisms.observable: the op is left disabled, with a warning, for a missing library, an unsupported world size, a non-MNNVL multi-node group, more than two PCIe-only GPUs or a failed P2P test; otherwise each rank shares IPC meta and buffer memory
mechanisms.note: The gate chain matches the code in order. same_node is an input rather than the probe, the max-size table is a fixed function of world size, and the MNNVL Lamport and multimem buffers are not allocated.

mechanisms.name: Custom all-reduce one-stage and two-stage kernels
mechanisms.trigger: should_custom_ar admits the tensor, chunked at max_size
mechanisms.observable: the C++ op takes 1-stage for 2 GPUs or small tensors (under 512 KiB to 4 GPUs, 256 KiB to 8), else 2-stage, unless VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO forces it
mechanisms.note: Kernel bodies are latency expressions, as the profile requires. The selection matches REDUCE_CASE.

mechanisms.name: Custom all-gather and reduce-scatter backends
mechanisms.trigger: all_gather or reduce_scatter on a TP group, and the sequence-parallel fused paths
mechanisms.observable: a size and topology gate picks legacy, mnnvl_lamport or mnnvl_multimem, or falls through to symm-mem or PyNccl
mechanisms.note: Backend choice runs and the kernels are latency models. Lamport epoch rotation and the lazy multimem buffer setup are not simulated, and nothing cites custom_collective_common.cuh.

mechanisms.name: GPU P2P capability probe and cache file
mechanisms.trigger: first custom all-reduce init on a node, unless VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK
mechanisms.observable: the local master spawns producer and consumer subprocesses per GPU pair, writes a cache file, and every rank reads it after a barrier; a failed pair disables custom all-reduce
mechanisms.note: Cache and local-master logic run. The IPC producer and consumer test in can_actually_p2p is reduced to one step, and the barrier is narrated.

mechanisms.name: FlashInfer all-reduce workspace and backend resolution
mechanisms.trigger: the first admitted tensor per hidden dim and dtype on a TP group
mechanisms.observable: auto resolves to mnnvl, falling back to trtllm on a single node and disabled on non-Blackwell multi-node; a shared workspace is created and reused, and a tensor the workspace cannot fit falls through to the next backend
mechanisms.note: A latency expression only. Admission is a config table in cuda-communicator.all-reduce, and backend resolution, the trtllm fallback, workspace creation and the buffer-size check are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: NCCL symmetric-memory all-reduce and allocator pool
mechanisms.trigger: VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM with 4 or more ranks and a tensor outside custom all-reduce's preferred range
mechanisms.observable: the input is copied into a symmetric pool buffer and reduced by NCCL; allocator compile and pool registration happen once per process
mechanisms.note: The size thresholds and the copy path run. The allocator compile, memory pool and context manager are absent.

mechanisms.name: Torch symmetric-memory communicator
mechanisms.trigger: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM on a TP group
mechanisms.observable: multimem or two-shot all-reduce over torch symmetric memory where the device, size and dtype qualify; also used for reduce-scatter and fused matmul reduce-scatter
mechanisms.note: Latency models reached by the dispatch. should_use_symm_mem and the init gates become a config flag.

mechanisms.name: PyNccl communicator: init, collectives, suspend, abort
mechanisms.trigger: communicator construction on any group with more than one rank; destroy at teardown
mechanisms.observable: an NCCL comm built from a store rendezvous runs in-place collectives; destroy aborts it on a daemon thread with a 5 s join, so graph-held comms cannot deadlock teardown
mechanisms.note: Collective latency and the disabled fallback exist. Init rendezvous, the abort thread and suspend/resume are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Device communicator suspend and resume across sleep
mechanisms.trigger: worker sleep and wake-up
mechanisms.observable: NCCL comm memory and FlashInfer all-reduce workspaces are released on suspend and restored collectively on resume; a missing ncclCommSuspend symbol skips with a warning
mechanisms.note: gpu-worker-impl.sleep models the memory allocator side only.

mechanisms.name: Distributed checkpoint prepare and restore
mechanisms.trigger: worker checkpoint_prepare and checkpoint_restore RPCs
mechanisms.observable: each device communicator tears down FlashInfer workspaces and the all2all manager, then rebuilds them over the process group on restore
mechanisms.note: Sets a checkpointed flag. No communicator, workspace or manager is touched.

mechanisms.name: CUDA graph capture context and buffer registration
mechanisms.trigger: capture of a CUDA graph with collectives
mechanisms.observable: a side stream is used inside TP, PP and DP capture contexts; custom all-reduce runs on registered buffers while capturing and registers them on exit
mechanisms.note: Custom all-reduce capture runs. The PP and DP contexts, FlashInfer PCIe and AITER captures and the warm-up empty_like path are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: QuickReduce all-reduce (ROCm)
mechanisms.trigger: ROCm MI300 with custom all-reduce enabled
mechanisms.observable: regime and quantization level are chosen by dtype and size, and a shared-buffer op handles tensors above the minimum size

mechanisms.name: AITER custom all-reduce and all-gather/reduce-scatter (ROCm)
mechanisms.trigger: ROCm with AITER custom all-reduce enabled, on TP groups and DP groups of size 2, 4 or 8
mechanisms.observable: AITER ops replace the custom all-reduce; DP attention dispatch and combine also use AITER all-gather and reduce-scatter

mechanisms.name: FlashInfer PCIe IPC all-reduce
mechanisms.trigger: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER_PCIE_IPC on a TP group
mechanisms.observable: a tuned IPC backend with an eager warm-up is chosen ahead of plain FlashInfer for tensors that qualify

mechanisms.name: CPU shared-memory, XPU and Ray PP communicators
mechanisms.trigger: platform selection of the device communicator and Ray compiled-graph PP
mechanisms.observable: CPU groups run SHM collectives when all ranks share a segment, XPU has its own fixed-rank-sum all-reduce, reduce-scatter and gather paths, and the Ray communicator wraps the PP group, mapping actors to ranks for compiled-graph sends

mechanisms.name: Shared-memory MessageQueue ring buffer
mechanisms.trigger: every RPC broadcast from the engine to workers, and every worker response
mechanisms.observable: one writer fills chunks and readers mark per-reader flags; a chunk is reused only once all readers have read it, a writer blocked past the timeout raises TimeoutError, and long waits log a message every interval
mechanisms.note: multiproc-executor.collective-rpc names the MessageQueue in a step title, as a broadcast and deadline, with no ring, flags or backpressure.

mechanisms.name: MessageQueue overflow and remote-reader path
mechanisms.trigger: a message over max_chunk_bytes, or a reader on another node
mechanisms.observable: an oversize message sets the overflow byte and travels over the local ZMQ socket; remote readers always receive over XPUB, and buffers of 1 MiB or more go out of band

mechanisms.name: MessageQueue construction and ready signal
mechanisms.trigger: executor start and each TP or PP group broadcaster
mechanisms.observable: the handle goes to the group, local readers attach to shm, remote readers subscribe, and wait_until_ready exchanges READY before the first message

mechanisms.name: Reader spin-then-idle wait
mechanisms.trigger: a reader waiting on an empty ring
mechanisms.observable: the reader busy-loops with sched_yield for 1 s after its last read, then idles on a conflated ZMQ notify; shutdown cancels the poll with a cancelled error

mechanisms.name: Zero-copy tensor arena for broadcast tensors
mechanisms.trigger: enqueue of CPU tensors when the queue has an arena
mechanisms.observable: tensors take a shared slot and readers get views; a slot frees when all readers release it, with a CUDA event gate on the pinned path, and a full arena falls back to out-of-band pickle

mechanisms.name: Same-node probe through shared memory
mechanisms.trigger: custom all-reduce init, MessageQueue construction, and the node-count helpers
mechanisms.observable: the source rank writes a magic message to a new segment and broadcasts its name; ranks that read it back count as same-node, and the result is all-reduced
mechanisms.note: Consumers take same_node as an input.

mechanisms.name: Multimodal SHM object store on the sender
mechanisms.trigger: a multimodal item with mm_processor_cache_type = shm
mechanisms.observable: a miss allocates in a single-writer ring and frees unused items FIFO on MemoryError; a hit returns an address handle, a too-large item goes uncached, and readers verify a signature
mechanisms.note: Allocation, FIFO eviction and caught errors run. Reader signature verification, monotonic id validation and the reader flag are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Model-parallel group layout and creation
mechanisms.trigger: worker init_device, once per process
mechanisms.observable: ranks are laid out as ExternalDP x DP x PP x PCP x TP; TP, PP, DP, EP, ETP, DCP, PCP and EPLB groups are built and logged, and a TP group gets a message-queue broadcaster
mechanisms.note: Layout, sizes, the use_all2all decision and the log line run. Inner-DP and engram DP groups, the stateless elastic path and device-group sharing are missing.

mechanisms.name: World group and torch.distributed init
mechanisms.trigger: worker init_device
mechanisms.observable: with DP > 1 the rank is offset and the world widened over a TCP master, the backend falls back to gloo if unavailable, and a second call asserts the same size
mechanisms.note: Rank offset, gloo fallback and the size assert run. The elastic stateless world, split-group process-group init and external launcher variants are missing.

mechanisms.name: Model-parallel teardown and memory cleanup
mechanisms.trigger: cleanup_dist_env_and_memory at shutdown or between engines
mechanisms.observable: groups are destroyed and their globals reset, the process group and optionally Ray shut down, then GC and GPU cache empty
mechanisms.note: Group state resets. Per-communicator destroy and the memory steps are not simulated.

mechanisms.name: StatelessProcessGroup over a TCP store
mechanisms.trigger: cross-process agreement before torch.distributed exists: EPLB, NCCL rendezvous, trainer groups
mechanisms.observable: send, receive and broadcast use counted store keys per sender; keys expire by TTL and all_gather and barrier build on broadcast
mechanisms.note: Send, receive and broadcast run. expire_data, all_gather_obj, barrier and create are missing.

mechanisms.name: StatelessGroupCoordinator and port allocation
mechanisms.trigger: elastic EP worlds, DP and EP groups
mechanisms.observable: groups rendezvous over ports allocated on a coordination store, without a torch default process group

mechanisms.name: PP stage handoff of intermediate tensors
mechanisms.trigger: every step on pipeline-parallel ranks
mechanisms.observable: metadata goes on the CPU group, then each tensor with an optional all-gather slice; async sends retain their tensors and are reaped FIFO on device-backend completion, and receives finish through deferred post-processing
mechanisms.note: The synchronous handoff and the all-gather slice run. isend, irecv and the _pending_isends reap are missing, and no behavior calls send-tensor-dict or recv-tensor-dict; scenarios enter them directly.

mechanisms.name: Patched fused scaled matmul reduce-scatter
mechanisms.trigger: torch.compile fusing a matmul with reduce-scatter on a TP group
mechanisms.observable: the patched op looks the group up and uses the symm-mem fused path, or falls back to matmul then reduce-scatter
mechanisms.note: One call chain; the fake-tensor shape checks are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: MoE all-to-all backend selection
mechanisms.trigger: EP group construction when use_all2all
mechanisms.observable: all2all_backend picks AgRs, DeepEP HT/LL/V2, MoRI, MoonEP, NIXL EP, FlashInfer NVLink one- or two-sided or passthrough; an unknown name raises ValueError
mechanisms.note: Selection records a manager name, and dispatch returns unchanged for every manager except AgRs.

mechanisms.name: Naive and all-gather/reduce-scatter MoE dispatch and combine
mechanisms.trigger: each MoE layer forward with an AgRs manager
mechanisms.observable: hidden states and top-k gather across EP ranks (TP and DP sub-groups by case), experts run, and outputs reduce-scatter back by chunk size
mechanisms.note: The AgRs path runs with comm-group and size logic. dispatch_router_logits and allocate_combine_input/combine_into_output are not separate paths.

mechanisms.name: DeepEP, MoRI, MoonEP and NIXL EP handles and buffers
mechanisms.trigger: the first MoE call for a config; EP resize; fault queries
mechanisms.observable: handles are cached by config kwargs, set_num_sms and buffer bring-up run once; NIXL EP connects and masks ranks across staged EP sizes, and query_fault and clean_buffers serve fault tolerance

mechanisms.name: FlashInfer NVLink one- and two-sided MoE
mechanisms.trigger: flashinfer_nvlink_* all2all backend
mechanisms.observable: the manager initializes a shared alltoall workspace, the one-sided path combines into a caller buffer, and workspaces checkpoint and restore

mechanisms.name: EPLB load window and rearrangement countdown
mechanisms.trigger: after every forward, by the model runner
mechanisms.observable: load accumulates per physical expert; near the rearrangement it enters a sliding window, dummy steps still count, balancedness logs at its interval, and at the interval rearrangement starts unless async is still running

mechanisms.name: EPLB rearrangement in sync mode
mechanisms.trigger: step counter reaches the interval, sync mode, or the profile run
mechanisms.observable: window loads are all-reduced to logical experts, the policy computes a new map, weights move layer by layer, and maps are committed on every rank; a dummy max-cost rearrangement reserves buffers in the profile run
mechanisms.note: Main path runs; rank_mapping and use_last_expert_load (elastic EP) are missing, as is the ROCm no-material-gain skip, by a stated choice.

mechanisms.name: Hierarchical expert rebalance policy
mechanisms.trigger: each rearrangement
mechanisms.observable: groups are replicated by load and packed across nodes and GPUs, then intra-GPU slots are preserved to reduce moves
mechanisms.note: Read at step level, not compared line by line against the packing arithmetic.

mechanisms.name: EPLB async worker with per-layer commit
mechanisms.trigger: rearrange_event on a thread and side stream, with enable async
mechanisms.observable: the thread runs the policy, transfers one layer per forward, publishes a pending result, and blocks on consumed_event while the main thread copies into the model; a rank that stopped rebalancing stops all via a coordinated flag
mechanisms.note: One layer per step and the commit run, but in the main thread: no thread, stream, consumed_event or coordinated stop, and drain_async is missing.

mechanisms.name: EPLB contention-free migration batches
mechanisms.trigger: eplb_config.migration_batching_enabled, with async EPLB
mechanisms.observable: moves coalesce by rank pair and first-fit edge coloring gives batches where a rank talks to at most one peer
mechanisms.note: The config field validates in eplb-config.init; nothing schedules batches.

mechanisms.name: Expert weight move through the buffer
mechanisms.trigger: each layer of a rearrangement
mechanisms.observable: experts staying or moving locally are copied to the buffer, remote ones go by P2P with balanced source assignment, and the buffer writes back to the new slots
mechanisms.note: Step-level comparison only, and the rank_mapping variants are missing.

mechanisms.name: EPLB communicator selection
mechanisms.trigger: EplbState add_model
mechanisms.observable: torch_nccl, torch_gloo, torch_xccl, pynccl or nixl is built on the EPLB group; stateless groups force pynccl with a warning, and unsupported dtypes or devices raise

mechanisms.name: NIXL EPLB remote metadata exchange
mechanisms.trigger: eplb communicator nixl, each transfer
mechanisms.observable: agents initialize remotes once, register all expert memory, exchange send metadata, post reads, wait, and finish on a barrier
mechanisms.note: execute is one rendezvous for every backend, so no NIXL-specific exchange runs.

mechanisms.name: NCCL_MAX_CTAS override for mega MoE with EPLB
mechanisms.trigger: startup with DP > 1, EPLB on an NCCL communicator and the deep_gemm_mega_moe backend
mechanisms.observable: NCCL_MAX_CTAS is forced to 8 unless set, avoiding a deadlock with cooperative launch

mechanisms.name: Elastic EP scaling state machine
mechanisms.trigger: POST /scale_elastic_ep, per engine
mechanisms.observable: each engine role (existing, new, remaining, removing) moves through prepare, KV size sync, ready, commit and complete; all ranks set a ready key and commit only when asked
mechanisms.note: The route and client validate and return. The worker side ends in elastic-ep-scaling-executor.execute, which has no steps, and no scenario enters it.

mechanisms.name: Standby groups and the switch to the new world
mechanisms.trigger: the prepare and commit phases of scaling
mechanisms.observable: standby world, DP, EP and EPLB groups are built next to the active ones, then swapped in; MoE configs are rewritten and retired groups destroyed in the background

mechanisms.name: Elastic EP weight transfer and new-worker warm-up
mechanisms.trigger: scale-up with new workers
mechanisms.observable: an existing rank broadcasts weights and the expert mapping to new ranks, which warm up and capture graphs before the switch; the engine syncs wave and step counters at the join

mechanisms.name: EPLB reshuffle around scaling
mechanisms.trigger: commit of scale-up, and before scale-down removes ranks
mechanisms.observable: expert loads rerun with a rank mapping so departing ranks hold nothing, and scale-up redistributes to new ranks

mechanisms.name: KV connector factory and HMA gate
mechanisms.trigger: engine and worker start with kv_transfer_config
mechanisms.observable: a module path wins over the registry, unknown names and empty module paths raise, and a connector without SupportsHMA is refused while HMA is on
mechanisms.note: Error paths match. External classes are not imported or checked for the kv_cache_config constructor, and the role split returns a name.

mechanisms.name: Scheduler-side KV connector hooks
mechanisms.trigger: scheduling waiting requests, finishing requests, and each step output
mechanisms.observable: match tokens, update after alloc, build metadata, update output and request_finished route to the configured connector
mechanisms.note: The dispatch covers Example, NIXL pull, MoRIIO, SimpleCPUOffload, MultiConnector and HiSparse. Mooncake, MooncakeStore, Offloading, LMCache, FlexKV, HF3FS and DecodeBench return not-modeled, and on-new-request is a no-op for NIXL.

mechanisms.name: Worker-side KV connector step
mechanisms.trigger: every execute_model with a connector
mechanisms.observable: metadata binds, loads start, layers wait and save in the attention path, then wait_for_save, finished sets, load errors and stats go back in the model output, and metadata clears
mechanisms.note: start-load-kv handles NIXL pull and Example only, and NixlPush returns loaded 0.

mechanisms.name: KV output aggregation across workers
mechanisms.trigger: each executor step
mechanisms.observable: a request counts as finished only when expected_finished_count workers report it; stats, worker metadata, events and invalid blocks merge, and failed receives surface only together with finished
mechanisms.note: The counting and merging match the code, but no behavior calls it: multiproc-executor.execute-model and sample-tokens do not run the aggregator, so it only runs from its own flow.

mechanisms.name: MultiConnector fan-out
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = MultiConnector
mechanisms.observable: the first child with matched tokens loads the request, a child still looking up returns None for all, save results merge with a key-clash error, and extra async saves raise the expected finished count
mechanisms.note: The None lookup path is not modeled, and children without a table entry are skipped.

mechanisms.name: Transfer topology across unequal TP and DCP
mechanisms.trigger: handshake with a remote engine and block mapping
mechanisms.observable: the local TP rank maps to remote ranks by the TP ratio, block size ratio and replication; DCP picks its source ranks
mechanisms.note: Handshake targets and ratios run. compute_tp_mapping (head slots and GQA dedup for reads) is absent.

mechanisms.name: KV cache spec sizing and merge
mechanisms.trigger: KV cache config build
mechanisms.observable: specs for full attention, MLA, sliding window, Mamba and sparse produce page size and blocks per request, and specs merge across layers with mismatch errors; transfer groups select blocks
mechanisms.note: Arithmetic is per spec, but not compared line by line for every spec class.

mechanisms.name: KV connector stats and Prometheus families
mechanisms.trigger: each worker step reports stats; the engine observes them
mechanisms.observable: transfer counts, durations and bytes aggregate per connector, log periodically and feed labelled Prometheus metrics, including NIXL failure and expiry counters
mechanisms.note: NIXL stats accumulate and drain. No Prometheus family or periodic log is modeled.

mechanisms.name: NIXL disaggregated prefill: decoder pull
mechanisms.trigger: a request with do_remote_prefill reaches the decode scheduler
mechanisms.observable: all prompt tokens but the decoder backoff count as external and async; the request parks in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS while a non-blocking READ runs, then resumes on finished_recving
mechanisms.note: The match and the parking run. Split DRAM and VRAM reads and the per-region read plan are not modeled, and the handshake runs synchronously.

mechanisms.name: NIXL prefill block lease
mechanisms.trigger: a prefill finishes by stop or length; every worker step sweeps
mechanisms.observable: blocks stay pinned until every consumer rank has read and notified, or the kv_lease_duration deadline passes (rebased onto the worker clock), then free with a warning and an expiry count
mechanisms.note: The pin and the expiry run. Consumer-notification counting and the clock rebase are missing, and an expiry is not counted separately.

mechanisms.name: NIXL heartbeat extending prefill leases
mechanisms.trigger: each decode step for requests waiting on a remote engine
mechanisms.observable: on_new_request tracks requests per engine; start_load_kv sends HB:<ids> to its agents, and the prefiller extends each lease to now + 2/3 of the lease duration
mechanisms.note: The receiver extension exists on the push path only. Nothing sends a heartbeat, on_new_request is a no-op for NIXL, and pull mode has no heartbeat branch.

mechanisms.name: NIXL agent handshake
mechanisms.trigger: first contact with a remote engine
mechanisms.observable: the decoder sends GET_META_MSG to the listener, receives agent metadata and a timestamp used to estimate a clock offset, validates compatibility and adds the remote agent; a queued request then starts, and failure fails it
mechanisms.note: Listener and hash run. The handshake is modeled inline with a clock offset of 0, and metadata validation is a stub of the real checks.

mechanisms.name: NIXL failed read to invalid blocks to recompute
mechanisms.trigger: a NIXL read errors, or a handshake or notification fails
mechanisms.observable: the request is reported failed and finished together, its local blocks go invalid, and the scheduler recomputes them; a failed notification leaves the prefiller to free on lease
mechanisms.note: The invalid-block path runs. Failure logging and failed-notification stats are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: NIXL invalid remote engine backoff and replacement
mechanisms.trigger: a failed read probes local metadata; a new engine appears at a known address
mechanisms.observable: an invalid engine fails reads fast and is released when drained, with doubling backoff on repeats; a replaced engine is released once nothing reads from it
mechanisms.note: Replaced-peer release runs. The metadata probe, invalidation backoff and repeat doubling are missing.

mechanisms.name: NIXL stale engine eviction
mechanisms.trigger: a new remote engine appears
mechanisms.observable: engines idle past engine_ttl (default 3600 s) with no in-flight transfer are cleaned up before a new one is registered

mechanisms.name: Prefix caching and hybrid regions during transfer
mechanisms.trigger: a NIXL read for a request with a local prefix hit, on hybrid or DCP models
mechanisms.observable: blocks already local are skipped per region and per DCP rank; Mamba, MLA and packed layers get their own region and block mapping, and a block size mismatch expands ids
mechanisms.note: read-blocks-for-req reads the blocks it is given.

mechanisms.name: Host buffer staging for non-GPU-direct platforms
mechanisms.trigger: a platform where NIXL uses host memory
mechanisms.observable: prefilled blocks copy to host before a read; on the decoder they copy back after a read, and a TP head layout may be fixed up
mechanisms.note: The scheduler queues reqs_need_save. The copies and post-processing are not modeled.

mechanisms.name: Bidirectional transfer: turn-2 readback
mechanisms.trigger: a prefiller resuming from blocks kept on the decoder
mechanisms.observable: the decoder keeps blocks for decoder_kv_blocks_ttl and exports the deadline; the prefiller pulls blocks above kv_recompute_threshold unless the deadline is within a 5 s margin, then recomputes
mechanisms.note: Threshold and deadline gate run. The clock offset is 0 and heartbeat exclusion is not modeled.

mechanisms.name: NIXL push mode: writer thread and registrations
mechanisms.trigger: NixlPushConnector: the decoder registers its blocks, the prefiller finishes
mechanisms.observable: the writer thread pairs PUSH_REG with finished blocks in either order and writes; the decoder completes when every producer rank has notified, and lease expiry evicts
mechanisms.note: Writer pairing, notification counts and request_finished run. The push scheduler's match, alloc and meta hooks and registration deadlines are missing, and the worker hooks are not reached through start-load-kv.

mechanisms.name: Mooncake P2P transfer
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = MooncakeConnector, per decode pull
mechanisms.observable: the decoder sends metadata per paired prefill rank; the sender waits for readiness up to VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, RDMA-writes coalesced regions and replies FINISH; errors and timeouts report per request
mechanisms.note: Worker pieces run from their own flows or scenarios, and the connector hooks do not reach them. The scheduler side is missing, and validation is reduced to a TP pair and a ready check.

mechanisms.name: Mooncake bootstrap server and registration
mechanisms.trigger: prefill worker start, on TP 0 of the designated engine
mechanisms.observable: a FastAPI server records dp, tp and pp addresses; workers register with exponential backoff, a retry with the same address succeeds, and a different one is a 400

mechanisms.name: Mooncake store lookup across groups and tiers
mechanisms.trigger: scheduling a waiting request with kv connector MooncakeStoreConnector
mechanisms.observable: the LookupKeyServer counts hits on store keys, coordinated across cache groups by a per-spec hit walk; a pending async lookup returns None so the scheduler retries
mechanisms.note: One flat count over keys with a RESET branch. The coordinator, partial hash hits, tail-key boundaries and async lookup are absent.

mechanisms.name: Mooncake store save path
mechanisms.trigger: scheduler build_connector_meta, then worker wait_for_save
mechanisms.observable: the scheduler builds store jobs (with partial tails and boundary state), the send thread dedups keys, puts by replication factor and reports events; finished saves are referenced and released
mechanisms.note: The step puts every block as one state write. No scheduler, dedup, partial tail or event is modeled.

mechanisms.name: Mooncake store pressure skip and retry
mechanisms.trigger: a put fails on capacity
mechanisms.observable: a pressure flag skips further jobs for a request, and retry tokens replay a failed put; a success clears the pressure

mechanisms.name: Mooncake store load path
mechanisms.trigger: a request with store hits
mechanisms.observable: the recv thread reads masked chunks per group into blocks, and errors report block ids and failed requests so the scheduler recomputes

mechanisms.name: Mooncake store config and client setup
mechanisms.trigger: store worker init, and the embedding store client
mechanisms.observable: size strings parse, env and JSON configs resolve, and a distributed store with its own transfer engine is set up for this host
mechanisms.note: Config parsing runs. Store layout selection and token databases are missing.

mechanisms.name: MoRIIO write-mode transfer
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = MoRIIOConnector in WRITE mode
mechanisms.observable: the decoder notifies the prefiller of allocated blocks; the writer defers until blocks are known, with a timeout, RDMA-writes, and completion notifies the decoder and frees blocks
mechanisms.note: Deferral, message handling and scheduler state run. Geometry planning, sealing, heterogeneous-TP acks and the layer layout are missing.

mechanisms.name: MoRIIO read-mode transfer and SQ-full backoff
mechanisms.trigger: READ mode decode
mechanisms.observable: the decoder posts RDMA reads; a transient send-queue-full status retries with exponential backoff capped at 50 ms; any other failure is terminal
mechanisms.note: The scheduler passes read metadata, but no worker read or backoff is modeled.

mechanisms.name: MoRIIO handshake and discovery heartbeat
mechanisms.trigger: worker start and first contact with a peer
mechanisms.observable: a listener serves engine and tensor metadata; a child process pings the proxy until stdin closes, and repeated ZMQ errors end it
mechanisms.note: Heartbeat send and listener run. The client side of the handshake and session building are missing.

mechanisms.name: HF3FS async save and load
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = HF3FSKVConnector
mechanisms.observable: save threads allocate pages from a metadata server, gather blocks, write, and confirm or release; load threads locate keys, read and scatter; failure counts and task timing are reported
mechanisms.note: Workers run only from flows, since no connector hook reaches them. The scheduler hooks at hf3fs_connector.py:687-880 are missing.

mechanisms.name: HF3FS metadata server page allocation
mechanisms.trigger: an HTTP call from a save or load worker
mechanisms.observable: per-rank page allocators give pages per key all-or-nothing, confirm commits or releases them, and lookups report existence and locations
mechanisms.note: Step-level comparison only.

mechanisms.name: Offloading connector lookup and load jobs
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = OffloadingConnector, scheduling a waiting request
mechanisms.observable: keyed lookup over chunks (prefix or sliding window) returns hit tokens or None to retry; hits become load jobs on the worker, and requests with in-flight jobs are delayed
mechanisms.note: tiering-offloading-manager.lookup and cpu-offloading-manager.lookup exist in scheduler-kv, but no connector scheduler calls them.

mechanisms.name: Offloading connector store jobs
mechanisms.trigger: each scheduler step after requests advance
mechanisms.observable: complete chunks (with aligned boundaries and partial tails) become store jobs, deferred to the start of the next step so token sampling is not delayed; finished requests flush their final blocks

mechanisms.name: Offloading block reuse fence and preemption flush
mechanisms.trigger: a block with a pending store is reused or a request is preempted
mechanisms.observable: jobs that hold the block flush to submission and the worker waits, so the block is not overwritten mid-store

mechanisms.name: Offloading config and canonical block mapping
mechanisms.trigger: offloading connector start
mechanisms.observable: chosen groups, hash size and chunk size derive from the KV cache config with errors on conflicting options; a canonical mapping gives a stable byte layout
mechanisms.note: Config arithmetic and errors run. Only the opaque fallback of the canonical mapping is modeled, and nothing uses the result.

mechanisms.name: Offloading events and metrics
mechanisms.trigger: store and lookup in the connector
mechanisms.observable: KV events on stored chunks and removal, placeholder hashes for partial tails, and Prometheus histograms for lookup delays and transfer bytes

mechanisms.name: SimpleCPUOffload connector hooks
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = SimpleCPUOffloadConnector
mechanisms.observable: scheduler hook wrappers look up CPU hashes, pin hits and load them; completed stores become CPU prefix hits; capacity is split per rank, with an optional lazy store
mechanisms.note: The hooks run in the scheduler path. Backend validation and worker store and load are in scheduler-kv and not compared here.

mechanisms.name: HiSparse host-to-GPU page residency and DMA
mechanisms.trigger: each step with kv_connector = HiSparseConnector
mechanisms.observable: the coordinator plans page transfers, and the worker waits on the host-write event, copies blocks, restores pages, submits DMA, sets row mirrors and updates residency
mechanisms.note: Init checks the host pool and alloc records a request. No transfer plan, event, DMA or residency runs.

mechanisms.name: HiSparse transfer stats
mechanisms.trigger: each worker step
mechanisms.observable: DMA counts, bytes and row mirrors aggregate and reach Prometheus

mechanisms.name: LMCache in-process connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = LMCacheConnectorV1
mechanisms.observable: hooks delegate to the LMCache adapter for lookup, retrieve and store by layer; KV events go up and load errors report blocks

mechanisms.name: LMCache multi-process connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = LMCacheMPConnector
mechanisms.observable: a scheduler adapter looks up, per-request trackers build store and retrieve metadata, and the worker adapter moves blocks

mechanisms.name: FlexKV connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = FlexKVConnectorV1
mechanisms.observable: hooks delegate to a FlexKV client, reporting finished requests and load errors

mechanisms.name: DecodeBench connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = DecodeBenchConnector, for benchmarks
mechanisms.observable: prompt blocks are filled with synthetic values without a real prefill, once per request or all at startup

mechanisms.name: Example file connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = ExampleConnector
mechanisms.observable: tensor files per prompt hash serve as an external cache: match finds a folder, load reads layers on the forward, and save writes them
mechanisms.note: Step-level comparison only.

mechanisms.name: Example hidden states connector
mechanisms.trigger: kv_connector = ExampleHiddenStatesConnector, on a pooling prefiller
mechanisms.observable: hidden states write asynchronously to files through a thread pool on a copy stream, are named in kv_transfer_params, and are freed when writes finish

mechanisms.name: KV events publisher with replay
mechanisms.trigger: the engine publishes each step's KV cache events
mechanisms.observable: a background thread sends batches with a sequence number over ZMQ PUB and buffers them; a replay request gets buffered batches from a sequence, then an END marker; shutdown sends a sentinel and drains
mechanisms.note: The error backoff on a failed send is not modeled. The publisher has no modeled feeder; it runs from flows.

mechanisms.name: KV event aggregation across workers
mechanisms.trigger: each step on connectors that emit events
mechanisms.observable: events are counted per worker and only those seen by all workers are returned; connector events merge up through the output aggregator
mechanisms.note: The common-event count is right, but no behavior feeds it.

mechanisms.name: Routed experts auxiliary output
mechanisms.trigger: a request with routed_experts sampling params, per step
mechanisms.observable: routed expert ids are captured by block, tails stage across steps, full blocks publish by hash to a store, and request output materializes on finish; rejected speculative tokens are dropped
mechanisms.note: Capture runs from its own flow. The scheduler connector, worker commit and publish steps are absent, so nothing reaches a request output.

mechanisms.name: Auxiliary output LRU block store
mechanisms.trigger: a background writer thread, for each step's published blocks
mechanisms.observable: new keys go to the LRU tail and the oldest unreferenced are evicted; a batch that cannot fit raises, and the error sticks and resurfaces on later calls

mechanisms.name: Weight update session on the inference side
mechanisms.trigger: POST /start_weight_update, /update_weights and /finish_weight_update (or LLM calls)
mechanisms.observable: start begins layerwise reloading, update loads each chunk, finish finalizes and synchronizes, and a failed chunk ends the session
mechanisms.note: The session rules are modeled, but the engine calls are stubs with no steps, and engine selection by backend is missing.

mechanisms.name: NCCL weight broadcast from trainer
mechanisms.trigger: backend nccl, each weight sync
mechanisms.observable: trainer and workers rendezvous on a store and form a group; the sender broadcasts each tensor (or packed buffers) and each worker loads it; a sync follows the end
mechanisms.note: Sender posts the HTTP calls and worker toggles layerwise state. No tensor is broadcast or loaded, packed or not.

mechanisms.name: CUDA IPC weight transfer
mechanisms.trigger: backend ipc
mechanisms.observable: trainer exports IPC handles per GPU UUID, a worker rebuilds tensors on its device and loads them; a missing UUID raises; packed mode imports a shared buffer

mechanisms.name: Sparse NCCL weight patches
mechanisms.trigger: backend sparse_nccl
mechanisms.observable: flat index and value tensors are broadcast per parameter and applied in place, after validation on the sender

mechanisms.name: M2N weight reshard
mechanisms.trigger: backend nccl_m2n
mechanisms.observable: trainer and worker exchange meshes and a destination plan; each parameter is resharded from trainer placements into worker buffers over an NCCL comm
mechanisms.note: Init-info validation and one type check only. No reshard runs.

mechanisms.name: Sharded RDT pull-based weight sync
mechanisms.trigger: backend sharded_rdt, each sync
mechanisms.observable: trainer gathers groups into a producer actor bounded by lookahead; consumers pull with NIXL in a ring, post-process on a background thread, and signal free_group; a stalled sync hits a liveness error
mechanisms.note: Lookahead bound, group order errors and the sticky processing error run. The pull, free barrier, liveness timeout and shared packs are missing.

mechanisms.name: Weight sync clients and engine registry
mechanisms.trigger: trainer calls during a sync
mechanisms.observable: an HTTP or Ray client drives start, update and finish on the server; each backend has engine and trainer factory entries, and unknown names raise
mechanisms.note: HTTP post and the trainer factory run. The Ray client, the worker factory and modelexpress are missing.

mechanisms.name: Encoder cache connector factory and hooks
mechanisms.trigger: engine and worker start with ec_transfer_config, then scheduling of multimodal requests
mechanisms.observable: the connector class resolves from a registry; has_cache_item, alloc, meta and finish hooks route on the scheduler, and save and load on the worker
mechanisms.note: Base role logic and Example save run. No factory is modeled, and hooks have no caller.

mechanisms.name: ECCPU NIXL grant, read and ack
mechanisms.trigger: a consumer with an announced remote encoder output
mechanisms.observable: a consumer sends XferReq and the producer grants or NACKs, pins blocks with a 30 s lease; the consumer reads, quarantines on timeout, and drains safely; a peer going down fails its reads
mechanisms.note: Only the server transport drain exists. No grant, lease, read or quarantine is modeled.

mechanisms.name: ECCPU admission and fallback
mechanisms.trigger: scheduling a multimodal request on the consumer
mechanisms.observable: an encoder waits on a remote read within a budget or falls back to local encoding, or fails the request, on a bad announced size, read failure or expiry
mechanisms.note: Alloc and meta run. _admit_item, the fallback and remote reads are missing.

mechanisms.name: ECCPU embedding cache and shared region
mechanisms.trigger: each encoder output on a producer or consumer
mechanisms.observable: a shared /dev/shm region holds blocks, pinned on GPU; entries allocate with eviction of unpinned, and pins hold during reads
mechanisms.note: Alloc does not evict, and worker copies are missing.

mechanisms.name: EC Mooncake producer push
mechanisms.trigger: a producer engine with a request carrying a transfer id
mechanisms.observable: reservations fan out to shards, source tensors stage, and pushes move through WAITING_INPUTS, WRITING, NOTIFYING and DONE, with cancel and failure paths
mechanisms.note: One step moves ready pushes to pushed. No state machine, reservation or write is modeled.

mechanisms.name: EC Mooncake consumer reservations
mechanisms.trigger: a producer asks to reserve a destination
mechanisms.observable: a reservation goes through WRITING, READY, CANCEL_PENDING, EXPIRE_PENDING and terminal states with a TTL; tombstones hold cancelled ids and a ready event reaches the scheduler
mechanisms.note: The control loop handles reserve, status, complete and cancel. TTL expiry, tombstones and deferred states are missing.

mechanisms.name: EC Mooncake scheduler transfer table
mechanisms.trigger: each scheduling of a consumer request
mechanisms.observable: each transfer goes from AVAILABLE to LOADING to READY; deadlines expire it, a timed-out load turns the request unavailable, and the request fails or encodes locally

mechanisms.name: EC Mooncake consumer memory pool
mechanisms.trigger: reservation and release of encoder outputs
mechanisms.observable: a contiguous allocator holds outputs, an LRU resident pool keeps released entries for reuse, and frees defer on a GPU event

mechanisms.name: Mooncake embedding store backend
mechanisms.trigger: encoder input resolution and encoder output save
mechanisms.observable: existing keys load directly and a failed lookup or get falls back to the encoder; saves enqueue contiguous tensors with a byte budget
mechanisms.note: Client creation only. No lookup, save or fallback is modeled.

mechanisms.name: EC connector stats and Prometheus families
mechanisms.trigger: each worker step
mechanisms.observable: transfer durations and bytes aggregate and go to logs and Prometheus
